https://www.surinenglish.com/malaga/mala.text: The picture of gender-based violence in Malaga so far this year is devastating. In just seven months, the province has seen six confirmed femicides, as reported by the government delegation against gender-based violence.With this tragic figure, Malaga has already reached the total number of femicides in 2025, when it broke its all-time record (2003) and topped the national map. It surpassed provinces such as Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia.In July alone, by far the deadliest month of the year, five women were found dead in the province with signs of violence, two of them this week within just 24 hours of each other. The latest case, which occurred on Tuesday, is pending confirmation. Sources, however, believe that the autopsy will confirm the gender-based nature of the murder.At the national level, the number of women murdered has now reached 31 (compared to 24 recorded at the end of July last year), nine of whom were killed in Andalucía (three more than in the same period last year). The diversity of variables such as nationality, age, romantic relationship, family responsibilities and socioeconomic level once again demonstrates the absence of a defined pattern: sexism strikes regardless of social status or origin.Two of the women murdered this year were named María and two others, Victoria. The other names are Cristina and Patricia. All were stabbed to death, except for one, who died after being shot. She was the only one who lived with her murderer (her husband) at the time of the incident. In two other cases, the perpetrators were ex-husbands, whom the victims had previously reported for domestic abuse. María, murdered this week in Antequera , had been registered in the VioGén system since 2023. It so happens that, just days before the crime, the court revoked her protection order after she had apparently requested it herself. The family of the 29-year-old woman, who leaves behind two orphaned children, suspect that she was coerced by her ex-partner into taking that step. The assailant took his own life after killing her.British-born Victoria, 33, was also murdered by her ex-husband , Juan Antonio, whom she had also reported to the police. Despite the restraining order, he repeatedly violated it. He had two prior convictions for minor threats and breach of a restraining order. Victoria was the first victim of gender-based violence in the province in 2026. Her ex-partner stabbed her to death on 26 January in front of her three children, who were between the ages of seven and eleven, in her home in Alhaurín el Grande. Later, the man turned himself in at the Alhaurín de la Torre prison and confessed to the crime.Almost five months later, in the early hours of 5 June, the bodies of Victoria, 51, and her husband, Francisco, 56, were found with gunshot wounds in their home in the Palma-Palmilla district in Malaga city. From the beginning, all hypotheses suggested that the man, who had been under psychiatric treatment and on sick leave for years, had killed her and then taken his own life with the same gun. In this case, neither of them was registered in the VioGén System.On 1 July, the body of 35-year-old Cristina, a resident of Malaga city's Ciudad Jardín district, was found in a well in Rincón de la Victoria . That same day, her ex-partner confessed that he had stabbed her to death weeks earlier.The man appeared in the VioGén system for three other previous victims. Both he and another individual, who allegedly helped him dispose of the body, remain in pretrial detention, while a woman has been released pending investigation.Just one week later, in the early hours of 8 July, a 61-year-old woman and her 31-year-old daughter were found dead in their home in Mijas after the house had been set on fire . Their names were María and Patricia, respectively. Both had stab wounds, leading investigators to suspect from the outset that the perpetrator had tried to disguise the double murder with arson.The following day, the mother's ex-partner, 67, was arrested for his alleged involvement in the double murder and for suspected robbery with violence . The man appeared in the police database as a "persistent aggressor".People who knew him well told SUR that he had been in prison several years prior for attempting to strangle a former partner.On Monday, the police discovered the body of 29-year-old María in her home in Antequera. Less than 24 hours later, 45-year-old Melinda, from Hungary, was was found stabbed to death in a home in Benahavís . Her case is the only one that has not yet confirmed a motive. Neighbours raised the alarm after hearing a loud assault and seeing a man flee in a vehicle. For now, the police only know that Melinda and her murderer knew each other.The province has recorded 68 femicides since 2003. January and July stand out as the deadliest months, with nine women murdered by their partners or ex-partners each. By age, the most affected group is the 18-30 (18 victims), followed by 41-50 (17) and 31-40 (12). There were also nine victims between the ages of 51 and 60, five between 61 and 70 and seven between 71 and 84.The other major victims are the orphans, who face a complex and painful process to regularise their family status, continue their studies or apply for assistance. Since 2003, the number of children orphaned by gender-based violence in the province has reached 29.Review the latest crime and judicial news reports

https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/11/two-.text: Two Azerbaijani sailors were killed when a tugboat was struck by drones in the Black Sea on Tuesday, in the latest attack on civilian shipping near the Ukrainian port of Odesa.The Somali-flagged tugboat TEDY, owned by Mert Marine Corporation, was first hit near Odesa before coming under two further drone attacks overnight as it sailed toward the Romanian port of Constanta.Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry confirmed the deaths of crew members Aslan Aliyev and Asim Gasimov. Two other Azerbaijani sailors, Imran Novruzov and Rauf Aliyev, were hospitalised in the Ukrainian city of Chornomorsk with burn injuries. Six further crew members received treatment at the scene.The vessel carried 10 crew members in total, including Azerbaijani, Turkish, German and Ukrainian nationals.Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry said it was coordinating with diplomatic missions and relevant authorities and was taking measures to repatriate the injured and carry out procedures relating to the deceased. It did not attribute responsibility for the attack.Ukraine's Ministry for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport said Russia had carried out the attack, describing it as part of a sustained campaign against civilian vessels and port infrastructure.Russia's Defence Ministry said on Wednesday it had struck two cargo vessels heading to Odesa and a tugboat, claiming the ships were carrying military supplies. Kyiv did not comment on the Russian claim.Chornomorsk is a major Ukrainian commercial port on the Black Sea and one of the principal terminals for Ukrainian grain exports.Following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022, Kyiv and Moscow negotiated the Black Sea Grain Initiative, which allowed Ukrainian agricultural exports to resume under UN and Turkish supervision before Russia withdrew from the agreement in July 2023.Russia has since targeted the port and its surrounding infrastructure repeatedly.Attacks on civilian shipping in the Black Sea have intensified since July, when multiple merchant vessels flying the flags of third countries have been struck, raising concern about the risk to seafarers.The attack on the TEDY is the latest in a series of incidents involving Azerbaijani sailors. Five Azerbaijani citizens were killed in attacks on two vessels in the Sea of Azov in June.

Photograph: Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters View image in fullscreen People shopping in a market still submerged in flood water in Bangkok, Thailand, on Monday. Photograph: Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters Weather tracker Flooding Analysis Bangkok declared a ‘disaster zone’ after flooding, as rainstorms shift direction James Parrish for MetDesk Capital city submerged in waist-high flood water, while elsewhere Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii’s Big Island Mon 28 Sep 2026 04.18 EDT Last modified on Mon 28 Sep 2026 06.37 EDT Share Bangkok was declared a disaster zone by its city officials towards the end of last week, after streets in Thailand’s capital city were submerged in up to waist-high flood water. The flooding stemmed from an active cell of low pressure across central Thailand that brought continuous heavy rainfall and thunderstorms to Bangkok and surrounding regions. The heavy rain began early on Thursday when the weak area of low pressure travelled north-westwards up the gulf of Thailand before then sitting over central Thailand by Friday morning. For most of the following two days this low pressure remained roughly in situ, which allowed unrelenting downpours over Bangkok and nearby areas. One weather station near Prachin Buri, just north-east of the capital, recorded 213.5mm within a 24-hour period between Friday and Saturday evening local time – for comparison, London receives an average 585mm a year ). Fortunately, the centre of the low-pressure cell shifted north-westwards on Sunday and brought an end to the torrential rainfall. 1:27 Bangkok residents navigate streets by boat as flood waters rise – video Out in the central Pacific, meanwhile, citizens of Hawaii’s Big Island were threatened by Hurricane Nolo over the weekend. The system initially approached the archipelago early last week, bringing heavy rainfall from around Tuesday evening. By the early hours of Saturday Nolo was a category 2 hurricane, with sustained windspeeds of 85-90knots (98-104mph), situated at its closest to the archipelago at approximately 145 miles (233km) south of the Big Island. Strong winds were not the only threat to the Big Island, as the vast quantity of rainfall raised concerns over flooding and mudslides. Since the impacts of Nolo started late on Tuesday 22 September, weather stations in the north-east of the island have received over 530mm of rainfall. Fortunately, Nolo has propagated westwards away from Hawaii where it is forecast to peak in its intensity on Monday 28 September, with current predictions of achieving category 4 status. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Down to Earth The planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential after newsletter promotion Meanwhile, farther east in the Pacific Ocean, Hurricane Polo is now forecast to make landfall with the Baja California peninsula late in the day on Monday 28 September. The once category 5 hurricane will downgrade to category 2 by landfall with sustained winds of 96-110mph. A hurricane warning has been issued in coastal regions due to the risk of a storm surge where winds are onshore. Polo will also bring intense downpours while traversing the peninsula with 100-200mm expected, potentially reaching up to 250mm locally. The bulk of this rain falling within a 12-hour period and bringing the risk of life-threatening flooding and mudslides. The storm will continue to weaken while propagating north-eastwards across the Sonora region in Mexico. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP View image in fullscreen Greens senator Jordon Steele-John has confirmed he has taken leave from parliament. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP Australian Greens Embattled Greens senator Jordon Steele-John confirms leave from parliament after allegations against him made public WA politician says he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be ‘unacceptable’ Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Sarah Basford Canales Fri 23 Oct 2026 20.52 EDT Last modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 20.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jordon Steele-John has confirmed he will not attend parliament next week as the embattled Greens senator releases a letter detailing the allegations against him. After days of confusion following historical complaints about alleged misconduct were publicly aired in the media, Steele-John posted a statement to social media late Friday night. In the statement, the Western Australian senator said he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be “unacceptable”. He will instead focus on seeing through an independent investigation to its conclusion, he said. “Over the past few days there has been a growing chorus calling on me not to attend parliament next week. I have explored attending digitally but have been informed that would also be unacceptable,” Steele-John said. Steele-John said a precedent of keeping parliamentarians out of parliament after “allegations of allegations” are made had now been set. “Had an allegation or complaint been made against me, I would have taken these actions immediately,” he said. The 32-year-old senator’s attendance in parliament for the remainder of the year had been uncertain after a public stoush with the party’s leader, David Shoebridge , over whether he was on leave while an investigation was undertaken into allegations he had acted inappropriately towards women between 2017 and 2025. The complaints are now subject to an independent investigation commissioned by the WA Greens and have been referred to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Commission . Shoebridge claimed Steele-John had requested leave and he accepted it last week after seven party members penned a letter to the leader urging an investigation into the claims. Jordon Steele-John’s position remains in limbo as Greens prepare for moment in spotlight Read more The three-page letter sent on 13 October, and first published by the Nine newspapers, said the authors had been “made aware of multiple allegations of serious misconduct” against Steele-John about his “behaviour in the presence of women”. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The letter referred to an allegation of sexual harassment at a Greens campaign event in 2024 that the alleged victim had not reported out of fear and backlash. The letter provided no further detail. In another, the authors referred to an allegation of “serious sexual misconduct” in 2025. Also contained in the letter was a reference to a disparaging nickname for Steele-John – “feels on wheels” – which the authors said implied he had a reputation for acting inappropriately. “To be clear, all signatories to this letter know that an allegation does not equate to a fact and/or guilt. We simply believe that it is in the party’s best interests to ensure that every allegation is investigated thoroughly, in alignment with community and member expectations,” the letter’s authors wrote. Steele-John was defiant in a lengthy statement last Sunday , rejecting the allegations against him, denying he agreed to take leave from parliament and accusing an internal faction within the Greens of playing “nasty political games” in their decision to release the letter to the media. Steele-John said any claims of his alleged behaviour should be investigated “fairly and thoroughly” but accused an “unofficial faction” within the WA branch had released the complaint letter to the media in a bid to oust him from the Senate. Guardian Australia has confirmed the WA police told Steele-John the investigation was closed in May with no charges.
